capitals.name: Frösön
capitals.note: The Jämtland page: the farthings had their own assemblies, 'all parallel with the common assembly on Frösön', and 'Frösön acquired the position as regional centre' (both undated); the Jamtamót page does not name the site. Reviewer eu-14-d (2026-10-31): seat sourced from the Jämtland page; the earlier placeholder label removed.

keyframe_review.note: 25,820 km2 round Storsjön, 61.76-64.20N. The pages give no borders. Infobox area (Jämtland page, the modern province, no year): 34,009 km2, ratio 0.76 to the shape, within a factor of two. The Jamtamót page: 'Founded in the first half of the 10th century' and 'the period before 1178 is regarded as a peasant republic'; the Jämtland page: 'Jämtland was originally an autonomous republic'. The start year 947 is Cliopatria's; the pages give only the half-century.

25,918 km2: the same land, 98 km2 larger (one cell on the western edge; the neighbouring Norwegian shape changes in the same years). No page dates anything in 1003 or 1015; the shape is kept as a Cliopatria boundary tweak.

25,820 km2, back to the 947 outline. The Frösö Runestone page dates the stone 'between 1030 and 1050' ('Austmðr, Guðfastr's son, had this stone raised and this bridge built and Christianized Jämtland'); the Jämtland page puts the Christianisation 'in the middle of the 11th century'. No change of frontier is dated; kept to 1176.

correction.text: the shape unchanged, valid for 1177 only: 'Jämtland was conquered by Norway in 1178'

keyframe_review.note: 25,820 km2 to 1187 in Cliopatria. The Jämtland page: 'conquered by Norway in 1178 and stayed Norwegian for over 450 years until it was ceded to Sweden in 1645'; the Jamtamót page: 'falling under Norwegian control with the loss at the Battle of Storsjön in 1178'. From 1178 the land belongs to old-kingdom-of-norway (its own dossier carries a 1178-1187 keyframe).

region.text: Jämtland round Storsjön: the land of the Jamts and their assembly, the Jamtamót

ledger.note: c. 947: the Jamts' assembly, the Jamtamót, governs Jämtland as a peasant republic. Jamtamót page: 'Founded in the first half of the 10th century, it was one of the oldest elected assemblies in the world'; 'The Jamtamót initially had no king over it'. Jämtland page: 'originally an autonomous republic' (no year). The year 947 is Cliopatria's; the page gives only the half-century, so the date is a bridge.

1178: Norway conquers Jämtland. 'Jämtland was conquered by Norway in 1178 and stayed Norwegian for over 450 years until it was ceded to Sweden in 1645'; the Jämtland page also has it 'defeated by king Sverre of Norway after losing the Battle of Storsjön'. Cliopatria keeps the row to 1187.

1178: the Jamts lose the Battle of Storsjön and the republic ends. Jamtamót page: 'The Jamtamót continued to operate after falling under Norwegian control with the loss at the Battle of Storsjön in 1178'. The land goes to the Old Kingdom of Norway (successors).

wars.name: Battle of Storsjön
wars.outcome: The Jamts lost the Battle of Storsjön in 1178 and Jämtland came under Norwegian control, where it stayed until 1645.
wars.note: The Jämtland page names King Sverre as the victor ('defeated by king Sverre of Norway after losing the Battle of Storsjön'); the Sverre of Norway page, opened for this, does not mention Jämtland (it has Sverre proclaimed king in Trøndelag in June 1177), and neither page gives the day or the place of the battle.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary of Jämtland; the shape follows the modern province's mountain and forest edges and is soft throughout.

sources.title: Jämtland

notes: Page budget 5 of 5 opened, all listed; the fifth (Jämtland County) was silent on the Middle Ages. A peasant republic and its assembly, 10th century to 1178, then Norwegian; Cliopatria's Jaemtland row (947-1187) runs nine years past the 1178 conquest, which two pages date (Jämtland, Jamtamót) and which old-kingdom-of-norway already enters as a 1178 gain with a 1178-1187 keyframe. The dossier therefore ends in 1178 (the shape is drawn through 1177; the 1178 year is shared with Norway) and the 1177 shape is valid for one year. START: 947 is Cliopatria's; the pages say 'first half of the 10th century' (the Jämtland page also ties the Jamtamót to the Althing of 930, marked 'citation needed'): confidence 1. NOT RECORDED because the pages give no year: the saga tribute ('sometimes paid taxes' to the Norwegian kings Håkon Adalsteinsfostre and Øystein Magnusson 'for protection', once to a Swedish king; the page calls the sagas' reliability 'low'), which could be a vassal tint of Norway; the Christianisation (stone 1030-1050; 'the middle of the 11th century'), which is not a territorial event. AREA: the shape's 25,820 km2 against the modern province's 34,009 km2 (ratio 0.76, within a factor of two); the shape misses the edges, and Härjedalen is not part of it. CAPITAL: none attested; Frösön is a label anchor from the runestone page, not from a source naming a seat. GAZETTEER: no names missing (Jämtland resolves as admin-1 of Sweden; Frösön and Storsjön are not used in region specs).
